heard: Astronomers mailed physical hard, drives to photograph our galaxy's terrifying center. Discovered in 1974, Sagittarius A is a supermassive black hole at our galactic center. It has a mass about four million times our sun, hidden behind thick cosmic dust. About 350 years ago, this quiet beast released a million times more energy than today. In 2017, the Global Event Horizon Telescope captured the glowing ring around its shadow. But gas orbits this small target so fast that its appearance changed in mere minutes. The resulting flood of scientific data was too massive to send over the internet. Instead, five years of complex processing finally revealed the direct image in May 2022. No network on Earth could easily transmit the secrets of our galaxy's lurking beast.
